status_summary: Executive Order 14307 (signed 2025-06-06) directed DOT and the FAA to propose a beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) drone rule within 30 days and to run an eVTOL integration pilot program; the FAA proposed the BVLOS rule on 2025-08-07, opened the pilot program on 2025-09-16 and selected eight projects spanning 26 states on 2026-03-09. Demonstration flights under the pilot program began in 2026, including Texas on 2026-09-10 and North Carolina on 2026-09-23. A trade report says the FAA sent the final BVLOS rule (Part 108) to OIRA on 2026-07-10, after missing a January 2026 statutory deadline; no final rule had been published in the Federal Register listings reviewed. The executive order does not create an interagency body for spectrum, drones and advanced air mobility, and no such clearinghouse was found.

timeline.event: President signs EO 14307, Unleashing American Drone Dominance (published 2025-06-11). It directs DOT and the FAA to propose a BVLOS rule within 30 days and finalize it within 240 days as appropriate, and to issue a request for proposals within 90 days for an eVTOL Integration Pilot Program with at least five projects. It relies on existing bodies for coordination and creates no new interagency clearinghouse.
FAA and TSA publish a proposed rule, Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations (document 2025-14992).

FAA announces the eVTOL and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) and requests proposals from state, local and tribal governments with private partners; proposals were due in December 2025.
FAA reopens the BVLOS proposed rule comment period for 14 days (to 2026-02-11) to better understand comments on ADS-B Out, electronic conspicuity and detect-and-avoid requirements.

DOT and the FAA select eight eIPP projects from more than 30 proposals, spanning 26 states; DOT says public operations should begin by summer 2026 and that test data will inform regulations for operating these aircraft at scale.

FAA notice implements the Section 927 waiver process for certain unmanned aircraft operations, an authority from the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 that lets the FAA waive certain rules instead of requiring rulemaking or exemptions.

FAA sends the completed BVLOS final rule (Part 108) to OIRA, according to Aerocorner; the report says Congress had set a January 2026 deadline that the FAA missed, and that the rule had not been published as of 2026-08-28.

DOT marks the launch of eIPP demonstration flights in Texas (BETA Technologies and Joby Aviation aircraft, with the Texas Department of Transportation); a similar launch followed in North Carolina on 2026-09-23.

title: Remove barriers to emerging aviation technology such as eVTOL aircraft and drones
uncertainties: The OIRA submission date of 2026-07-10 and the missed January 2026 deadline come from a single trade report; the OIRA (reginfo.gov) docket was not checked, and Federal Register listings through 2026-10-07 showed no final BVLOS rule. The count of eIPP launch sites is inconsistent between the two DOT launch releases, so no ordinal is stated. The FAA's broader certification performance (for example powered-lift type certification) was not researched, so the 'certify new technology faster' recommendation is only partly measured. The FCC's 2026-04-16 notice titled Unleashing American Drone Dominance appeared in a Federal Register search but was not read.
